## plugin:datadog:mcp
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). Consult Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. ## plugin:honeycomb:honeycomb

<role>
You are an observability assistant for Honeycomb users. You investigate production behavior — performance, errors, deployment impact, alert state — by querying real telemetry through these tools. The workspace's actual state is only knowable through tool calls; do not reason from priors about what services, datasets, or alerts exist.

When the user names a dataset, span, or service, treat it as a starting point for discovery, not a license to skip it. The right span name within a dataset is rarely obvious from the dataset name alone, and aggregating the wrong attribute or the wrong span is the most common cause of misleading answers.
</role>

<workflow>
For most observability questions — including "how many", "what's slow", "what's erroring" — start with span discovery (list_spans, get_span_details). Reach for run_query only when you need a calculation, distribution, or comparison those tools can't express. Span tools work across all trace-aware datasets in scope without needing to know which dataset to target.

# 1. The "ref backend" concept

## Overview
The codebase has a pluggable **checkpoint storage backend** system. Checkpoints (the persistent record of AI sessions) can be stored via different backends selected through a registry. The "ref backend" you're referring to is the **git-refs backend** (`git-refs`), one of two built-in git-backed backends. There are two axes of storage:

- **Ephemeral (temporary)**: shadow branches (`entire/<commit-hash>`) — intra-session rewind. This is NOT pluggable; it's always the git shadow-branch store (`ephemeralStore`). See `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/store.go:40-60` and `checkpoint.go:49-59`.
- **Persistent (committed)**: the permanent checkpoint record. This IS pluggable via the backend registry.

## The two built-in persistent backends
Defined in `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/registry.go`:

- **`BackendTypeGitBranch = "git-branch"`** (registry.go:19) — the default. Stores all checkpoints on a single git branch `entire/checkpoints/v1`, nested under `<shard>/<id>/`. Implemented by `GitStore` (`store.go:29-38`, factory at `registry.go:122-131`). Uses legacy 12-hex checkpoint IDs.
- **`BackendTypeGitRefs = "git-refs"`** (registry.go:27) — the "ref backend". Stores **one git ref per checkpoint** at `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>` (ref prefix defined in `refs_naming.go:16`). Each ref points at a commit whose tree root IS the checkpoint's contents. Implemented by `gitRefsStore` (`refs_store.go:32-42`, factory at `registry.go:136-148`). Uses ULID checkpoint IDs.

Both are `gitBacked: true` (registry.go:66-67). The registry is a `map[string]registeredBackend` (registry.go:59-69). `registeredBackend` (registry.go:44-57) holds a `factory Factory` plus a `gitBacked bool` capability flag.

**`gitBacked` semantics (registry.go:47-56):** Only git-backed backends may be the **primary**, because the whole checkpoint lifecycle (resume bootstrap, doctor reconcile, explain tree-read, push, cleanup, pre-push OPF) drives the primary's record through the repo/refs. Non-git backends can only be **mirrors**.

## The backend interface (the contract)
The core interface a backend implements is **`PersistentStore`**, defined in `api/checkpoint/interfaces.go:30-34`:
```go
type PersistentStore interface {
	CheckpointReader   // Read, List
	SessionReader      // ReadSessionContent, ReadSessionMetadata, ReadSessionPrompts, ReadSessionMetadataAndPrompts
	Writer             // Write(ctx, WriteRequest)
}
```
- `CheckpointReader` (interfaces.go:13-16), `SessionReader` (interfaces.go:19-24), `Writer` (interfaces.go:80-82).
- `WriteRequest` (interfaces.go:45-76) is a sealed union: `Session`, `SessionTranscript`, `SessionSummary`, `CheckpointAttribution`. Backends dispatch on the concrete type (see `gitRefsStore.Write` at `refs_store.go:57-70` and `GitStore.Write` at `persistent_write.go:11-24`).
- Optional capability: `AuthorReader` (`persistent.go:2472`), implemented by both git stores.
- These are re-exported into the `checkpoint` package via type aliases in `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/aliases.go:16-51`.

The **factory** signature is `Factory func(ctx, env OpenEnv, cfg json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error)` (registry.go:41). `OpenEnv` (registry.go:32-37) carries `Repo`, `BlobFetcher`, `RefFetcher`, `Refs`. `Register(typ, f)` (registry.go:75-82) adds non-git backends as mirror-only.

A worked reference example of a **non-git backend** exists: `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/fsstore/fsstore.go` (JSON files on disk). It is test-only — registered via `registerForTesting()` in `fsstore/register_test.go:26-32` under type `"fs"` with a config block `{Path string}`. Production code has no way to register it.

## How the backend is selected/configured
Selection lives in **`cmd/entire/cli/settings/checkpoints.go`**:

- **`CheckpointsConfig`** (checkpoints.go:35-38): `{ Primary BackendConfig; Mirrors []BackendConfig }`.
- **`BackendConfig`** (checkpoints.go:43-46): `{ Type string; Config json.RawMessage }` — a discriminated selector; `Config` is the opaque per-backend options block passed to the factory.
- **`LoadCheckpointsConfig(ctx)`** (checkpoints.go:66-104) resolves the config. It is deliberately **fail-soft**: missing file / syntax error / unrelated invalid fields all resolve to `nil` → default git-branch backend. It errors only when a present `checkpoints` block is itself invalid. `settings.local.json` replaces `settings.json` wholesale (checkpoints.go:77-84). Uses `DisallowUnknownFields` (checkpoints.go:96) so it is NOT forward-compatible — adding a field is a coordinated reader-before-writer rollout.
- **Env overrides** (checkpoints.go:26-29, 141-153): `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_PRIMARY` and comma-separated `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_MIRRORS` fully replace any file config. These are the primary mechanism used today for e2e/CI/rollout (e.g. `integration_test/backend.go:36-38` iterates `git-branch`/`git-refs` by setting these).

## How selection flows into construction
`checkpoint.Open(ctx, repo, opts)` in **`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/open.go:63-97`** is the single wiring point:
1. Calls `settings.LoadCheckpointsConfig(ctx)` (open.go:67).
2. `resolvePrimaryType(cfg)` (open.go:120-127) → defaults to `git-branch` when nil.
3. `buildPrimary` (open.go:141-150) — rejects non-git-backed primaries.
4. `buildMirrors` (open.go:160-181) — one-of-each-type rule (each backend type may appear at most once across primary+mirrors).
5. Wraps in `newFanoutStore(primary, mirrors)` (`fanout.go:26-36`) — reads from primary, best-effort writes fanned out to mirrors (mirror failures logged & swallowed, `fanout.go:70-81`).
6. Wraps that in `newKindRoutingStore(...)` (`routing_store.go:37-45`) — routes **reads** by checkpoint ID kind so a repo mid-migration reads both formats: ULID → refs store; hex → branch store (and, under a refs primary, falls back to branch). Writes are NOT kind-routed; they go to the configured primary+mirrors.

**ID minting is backend-coupled**: `checkpoint.GenerateCheckpointID(ctx)` (`generate.go:19-25`) mints a ULID when `PrimaryIsRefs(cfg)` is true, else a legacy hex ID. `PrimaryIsRefs(cfg)` (`open.go:36-38`) = `cfg != nil && cfg.Primary.Type == "git-refs"`.

**Backend-aware call sites** (consumers of `PrimaryIsRefs`):
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_push.go:52` — git-refs primary pushes per-checkpoint refs (`prePushCheckpointRefs`) via a push queue (`refs_store.go:104-129`, `pushqueue.go`) instead of the v1 branch.
- `cmd/entire/cli/attach.go:521` — backend-aware fetch (git-refs fetches one checkpoint ref; git-branch pulls the v1 branch). See surrounding comments attach.go:552-625.
- `cmd/entire/cli/explain_export.go:206`.

## Committed-ref topology
`PersistentRefs` (`persistent_refs.go:13-17`) = `{Primary, Read, Push}`. `DefaultV1Refs()` (persistent_refs.go:20-27) points all three at the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. `ResolveRefs(ctx)` (persistent_refs.go:47-49) currently always returns the v1 topology. This topology applies to the git-branch backend; the git-refs backend resolves each checkpoint's own ref instead and ignores `env.Refs` (registry.go:133-135).

---

# 2. How `entire enable` currently works

## Command definition
`newEnableCmd()` in **`cmd/entire/cli/setup.go:781-965`**, registered in `root.go:107`. Flags/options struct `EnableOptions` at `setup.go:60-77`. Notable existing flags (setup.go:924-951): `--local`, `--project`, `--agent`, `--force`, `--skip-push-sessions`, `--checkpoint-remote`, `--telemetry`, `--absolute-git-hook-path`, `--search-skill`, `--agent-help-skill`, `--yes`, plus bootstrap flags (`--init-repo`, `--repo-name`, etc.). **There is NO backend-selection flag.**

## RunE flow (setup.go:798-921)
1. **Bootstrap if not a git repo** (setup.go:820-857): offers `git init` + optional GitHub repo creation (two-phase: init before agent setup, initial commit + `gh repo create` + push after).
2. Validate flags; discover external agent plugins (setup.go:859-866).
3. **`--agent <name>`** → non-interactive single-agent path `setupAgentHooksNonInteractive` (setup.go:874-884).
4. **Already set up** (`settings.IsSetUpAny`) → setup.go:888-917: apply any strategy/agent-management flags, then if already enabled just print status, else `runEnable` (the lightweight re-enable).
5. **Fresh repo** → `runSetupFlow` (setup.go:920).
6. After success (deferred): `reportRepoEnabled` (setup.go:967-1029) — best-effort API call telling the backend which repo was enabled (for web onboarding / trails).

## The core setup: `runEnableInteractive` (setup.go:1084-1232)
This is where everything is installed/written:
1. `firstRun` captured before writing anything (setup.go:1088).
2. Uninstall hooks for deselected agents (setup.go:1091).
3. **Install agent hooks** for each selected agent via `setupAgentHooks` → `hookAgent.InstallHooks(...)` (setup.go:1096-1099, 1393-1405). Optionally install search/agent-help skills.
4. `setupEntireDirectory(ctx)` — creates `.entire/` (setup.go:1109).
5. **Load + mutate settings** (setup.go:1113-1136): sets `Enabled=true`, `LocalDev`, `AbsoluteGitHookPath`, auto-enables `ExternalAgents` if any external agent, applies strategy options (`opts.applyStrategyOptions` at setup.go:80-101 — writes `strategy_options.push_sessions` and `strategy_options.checkpoint_remote`).
6. Determine target file (`settings.json` vs `settings.local.json`) and **save settings** via `saveSettingsToTarget` (setup.go:1138-1161).
7. **Install git hooks** via `strategy.InstallGitHook(ctx, silent, localDev, absolutePath)` (setup.go:1165) and `CheckAndWarnHookManagers` (setup.go:1168).
8. Optional Vercel prompt; telemetry consent; save again (setup.go:1178-1203).
9. **`strategy.EnsureSetup(ctx)`** (setup.go:1205).
10. Offer session import on first run (setup.go:1211); print "Ready."

## Git hooks installed
From `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/hooks.go`:
- `gitHookNames = ["prepare-commit-msg", "commit-msg", "post-commit", "post-rewrite", "pre-push"]` (hooks.go:31).
- `InstallGitHook` at hooks.go:290. Hook command bodies built around hooks.go:177-234; respects `core.hooksPath` (hooks.go:61, 124). The `pre-push` hook does not swallow exit codes because it runs the OPF pre-push flow (hooks.go:181).

## Settings written during enable
Only these fields get written: `enabled`, `local_dev`, `absolute_git_hook_path`, `external_agents`, `telemetry`, `strategy_options` (`push_sessions`, `checkpoint_remote`), and agent hook files. Save helpers: `SaveEntireSettings`/`SaveEntireSettingsLocal` (`config.go:41`, `config.go:49`) and `saveSettingsToTarget` (`setup.go:349`).

## Is there any backend choice during enable?
**No.** I confirmed via grep that:
- No code path writes the `settings.Checkpoints` field or a `"checkpoints"` JSON block anywhere in production code (only `LoadCheckpointsConfig` reads it, and env vars / manual editing set it).
- No enable/setup/wizard prompt references `git-refs`, `git-branch`, `primary`, or backend selection.

So today the git-refs backend can only be turned on by (a) setting `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_PRIMARY=git-refs` in the environment, or (b) hand-editing `.entire/settings.json` (or `.local.json`) to add a `"checkpoints": { "primary": { "type": "git-refs" } }` block.

---

# 3. Settings package — backend-related fields

In **`cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go`**:
- `EntireSettings.Checkpoints *CheckpointsConfig `json:"checkpoints,omitempty"`` (settings.go:151, comment 147-150). It exists on the struct so the strict `Load` (which uses `DisallowUnknownFields`) accepts the key; the actual consumer is the lenient `LoadCheckpointsConfig`.
- No other backend/storage-mode field exists. (`SignCheckpointCommits` at settings.go:145 is unrelated; `Strategy` at settings.go:155 is deprecated/ignored.)

The `CheckpointsConfig` / `BackendConfig` types and all load/validation logic live in the sibling file `cmd/entire/cli/settings/checkpoints.go` (detailed above).

---

# Implications for designing an "enable ref backend" path

Everything needed to *run* the git-refs backend already exists and is wired end-to-end (registry, store, ID minting, read routing for coexistence/migration, backend-aware push and fetch). What's missing is a **writer** of the config. Two clean insertion points:

- **Existing repo (`entire enable` re-run / a new subcommand or flag):** write `settings.Checkpoints = &CheckpointsConfig{Primary: BackendConfig{Type: "git-refs"}}` and persist via the existing `saveSettingsToTarget` / `SaveEntireSettings` path. Because `GenerateCheckpointID` and read-routing already handle mixed hex/ULID repos, flipping the primary on an existing repo is safe — old hex checkpoints stay readable on the v1 branch, new ones become ULID refs.
- **Initial enable:** add a backend choice to `EnableOptions` (setup.go:60) and set the field in `runEnableInteractive` right where other settings are mutated (setup.go:1119-1136), before `saveSettingsToTarget` (setup.go:1156).

Watch-outs: `LoadCheckpointsConfig` uses `DisallowUnknownFields` (checkpoints.go:96) so any new sub-field is a coordinated rollout; the one-of-each-type mirror rule (open.go:160-181); and only git-backed types may be primary (open.go:146-148). A git-branch mirror alongside a git-refs primary is explicitly contemplated in comments (registry.go:22-26) but mirror-push for downgrade safety is noted as "a later step" (manual_commit_push.go:49-50).</result>

Here's the lay of the land, then concrete suggestions.

## The key insight

The git-refs backend is **already fully wired and runnable** — registry, store, ULID minting, read-routing for mixed repos, backend-aware push/fetch all exist. The *only* thing missing is a **config writer**. Today it's turned on only via `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_PRIMARY=git-refs` or hand-editing `.entire/settings.json`.

So "enable the ref backend" reduces to: write `checkpoints.primary.type = "git-refs"` into settings and persist it through the existing save path. And crucially — **flipping an existing repo is already safe**: `GenerateCheckpointID` mints ULIDs going forward while `newKindRoutingStore` keeps reading old hex checkpoints off the v1 branch. There's no data migration to write. That's what makes a "simple path" realistic.

## Suggestions

**Option 1 — One shared flag on `enable` + `configure` (recommended)**
- `entire enable --checkpoint-backend refs` handles the **initial** case (set `EnableOptions.CheckpointBackend`, write `settings.Checkpoints` in `runEnableInteractive` right where other settings mutate, before `saveSettingsToTarget`).
- `entire configure --checkpoint-backend refs` handles the **existing-repo** case. This matches the documented layout exactly — `configure` is the canonical home for non-agent settings (telemetry, hook mode, strategy options), and backend selection is precisely that.
- Both call one tiny helper: validate the value against the checkpoint registry (must exist + be `gitBacked` to be primary), set the field, save to the right target file.
- Why this is the simplest: `enable` *already* has an "already set up" re-run branch that applies strategy flags, so even `enable --checkpoint-backend refs` alone works on an existing repo — `configure` just gives it a conventional home.

**Option 2 — A dedicated subcommand under the `checkpoint` group**
- `entire checkpoint backend show` (prints current + effective source: file vs env vs default) and `entire checkpoint backend set refs`.
- Best **discoverability** and it gives you a read path for free (useful for `doctor`/support). Natural fit under the existing `checkpoint` noun group.
- Slightly more surface than Option 1. Good candidate to advertise via `entire labs` while the backend is still rolling out, rather than exposing it in root help.

**Option 3 — Interactive prompt in the enable wizard**
- Add a Select to the wizard. Lowest-ceremony for humans, but per the agent-safe-fallbacks rule it's **only sugar on top of a flag** — you'd still need Option 1's flag for non-interactive/agent use. Probably premature to prompt *everyone* while this is experimental; I'd skip it for now.

My recommendation: **Option 1** as the core (one flag, one helper, both scenarios), optionally add Option 2's `checkpoint backend show` for a read/verify path. That's the minimal thing that's convention-correct and covers both entry points.

## Watch-outs to bake in

- **Value naming**: expose friendly `branch`/`refs` (or accept the raw `git-branch`/`git-refs`) and map to the registry type — don't invent a third vocabulary.
- **Validate as primary**: reject non-git-backed types as primary (they're mirror-only); reject unknown types with a message listing valid ones.
- **Target file**: reuse `saveSettingsToTarget` so `settings.local.json` vs `settings.json` is respected — `LoadCheckpointsConfig` treats `.local.json` as a wholesale replacement.
- **Forward-compat**: `LoadCheckpointsConfig` uses `DisallowUnknownFields`, so only write fields current readers understand.
- **Downgrade isn't symmetric yet**: refs→branch mirror-push for downgrade safety is noted as "a later step." Enabling refs forward is safe; if you want a safety net, allow an optional `git-branch` mirror alongside the refs primary (the one-of-each-type rule permits it).

17	// ErrInvalidCheckpointsConfig is returned when a present "checkpoints" settings
18	// block is malformed (e.g. a backend with no type).
19	var ErrInvalidCheckpointsConfig = errors.New("invalid checkpoints config")
20	
21	// Environment overrides for checkpoint backend selection. When EnvCheckpointsPrimary
22	// is set, it (and the optional comma-separated EnvCheckpointsMirrors) fully
23	// replaces any checkpoints block in settings — env wins over file, matching the
24	// other ENTIRE_* overrides (ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL, ENTIRE_TOKEN, …). Primarily for
25	// driving e2e/CI and rollout against a specific backend without editing settings.
26	const (
27		EnvCheckpointsPrimary = "ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_PRIMARY"
28		EnvCheckpointsMirrors = "ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_MIRRORS"
29	)
30	
31	// CheckpointsConfig selects checkpoint storage backends: one primary (source of
32	// truth, serves all reads and writes) and zero or more mirrors (independent
33	// backends that receive best-effort write fan-out). When absent, the checkpoint
34	// layer defaults to the built-in git-branch backend with no mirrors.
35	type CheckpointsConfig struct {
36		Primary BackendConfig   `json:"primary"`
37		Mirrors []BackendConfig `json:"mirrors,omitempty"`
38	}
39	
40	// BackendConfig is a discriminated backend selector: Type names the registered
41	// backend and Config carries the backend-specific options block (opaque here,
42	// decoded by the backend factory).
43	type BackendConfig struct {
44		Type   string          `json:"type"`
45		Config json.RawMessage `json:"config,omitempty"`
46	}
47	
48	// checkpointsEnvelope extracts only the "checkpoints" key, leaving every other
49	// settings field untouched so unrelated malformed/unknown settings cannot break
50	// checkpoint backend resolution.
51	type checkpointsEnvelope struct {
52		Checkpoints json.RawMessage `json:"checkpoints"`
53	}
54	
55	// LoadCheckpointsConfig reads the checkpoint backend selection from settings
56	// without the strict whole-settings validation that Load performs. It is
57	// deliberately fail-soft: a missing settings file, a whole-file JSON syntax
58	// error, or unrelated invalid fields all resolve to "no checkpoints config"
59	// (nil), so checkpoint construction falls back to the default git backend. It
60	// errors only when a "checkpoints" block is present but itself invalid.
61	//
62	// Precedence mirrors Load: a "checkpoints" block in settings.local.json
63	// replaces the one in settings.json wholesale (this is a selection config, not
64	// a deep-merged document). Clone preferences carry no checkpoint config and are
65	// not consulted.
66	func LoadCheckpointsConfig(ctx context.Context) (*CheckpointsConfig, error) {
67		// Env override wins over any settings file (precedence like ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL).
68		if cfg, ok := checkpointsConfigFromEnv(); ok {
69			if err := cfg.validate(); err != nil {
70				return nil, err
71			}
72			return cfg, nil
73		}
74	
75		base, local := checkpointsSettingsPaths(ctx)
76	
77		// "local replaces base wholesale": prefer a checkpoints block from local
78		// settings; fall back to base only when local has none. We extract the raw
79		// blocks fail-soft, then decode/validate just the one that wins — so a
80		// malformed block in the overridden file never blocks the file that wins.
81		raw, src := rawCheckpointsBlock(ctx, local), local
82		if raw == nil {
83			raw, src = rawCheckpointsBlock(ctx, base), base
84		}
85		if raw == nil {
86			return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // no checkpoints block present => default git backend
87		}
88	
89		var cfg CheckpointsConfig
90		dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(raw))
91		// DisallowUnknownFields surfaces typos (e.g. "primry") instead of silently
92		// ignoring them. The trade-off is that this CLI is not forward-compatible
93		// with checkpoints fields added by a newer CLI: an unknown field errors here.
94		// Adding a field is therefore a coordinated rollout — ship the reader before
95		// any writer emits the field. The error below points users at that cause.
96		dec.DisallowUnknownFields()
97		if err := dec.Decode(&cfg); err != nil {
98			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w in %s: %w; an unrecognized field can also mean this file was written by a newer CLI — confirm you are on the latest version", ErrInvalidCheckpointsConfig, src, err)
99		}

102		}
103		return &cfg, nil
104	}

107	// nil when the file is absent/unreadable, has a whole-file syntax error, or has
108	// no checkpoints block. It never errors: unrelated breakage in a settings file
109	// must not block checkpoint construction (the strict Load path surfaces it for
110	// normal commands).
111	func rawCheckpointsBlock(ctx context.Context, filePath string) json.RawMessage {
112		data, err := readConfined(filePath)
113		if err != nil {
114			if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
115				// A non-ENOENT read error (bad perms, settings.json is a directory or
116				// an escaping symlink, etc.) is a broken/untrusted setup; stay
117				// fail-soft so checkpoint construction defaults to git rather than
118				// newly failing resume/explain/hooks.
119				logging.Debug(ctx, "checkpoints config unreadable; defaulting to git backend",
120					slog.String("path", filePath), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
121			}
122			return nil
123		}
124	
125		var env checkpointsEnvelope
126		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &env); err != nil {
127			// Whole-file parse failure is unrelated breakage; stay fail-soft.
128			return nil
129		}
130		if len(env.Checkpoints) == 0 {
131			return nil
132		}
133		return env.Checkpoints
134	}
135	
136	// checkpointsConfigFromEnv builds a CheckpointsConfig from the environment when
137	// EnvCheckpointsPrimary is set. Mirrors are taken from EnvCheckpointsMirrors as a
138	// comma-separated list of backend types (no per-backend config blocks — the env
139	// override is for backend selection only). Returns ok=false when no primary is
140	// set, leaving file-based resolution in charge.
141	func checkpointsConfigFromEnv() (*CheckpointsConfig, bool) {
142		primary := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(EnvCheckpointsPrimary))
143		if primary == "" {
144			return nil, false
145		}
146		cfg := &CheckpointsConfig{Primary: BackendConfig{Type: primary}}
147		for _, m := range strings.Split(os.Getenv(EnvCheckpointsMirrors), ",") {
148			if t := strings.TrimSpace(m); t != "" {
149				cfg.Mirrors = append(cfg.Mirrors, BackendConfig{Type: t})
150			}
151		}
152		return cfg, true
153	}
154	
155	func (c *CheckpointsConfig) validate() error {
156		if c.Primary.Type == "" {
157			return fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoints.primary.type is required", ErrInvalidCheckpointsConfig)
158		}
159		for i, m := range c.Mirrors {
160			if m.Type == "" {
161				return fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoints.mirrors[%d].type is required", ErrInvalidCheckpointsConfig, i)
162			}
163		}
164		return nil
165	}

169	func checkpointsSettingsPaths(ctx context.Context) (base, local string) {
170		if worktreeRoot, ok := worktreeRootFromContext(ctx); ok {
171			return worktreeSettingsPaths(worktreeRoot)

173		return settingsAbsPaths(ctx)

15	// BackendTypeGitBranch is the built-in git-branch checkpoint backend: it stores
16	// the committed record on a git branch (entire/checkpoints/v1) in this repo. It
17	// is git-backed (see registeredBackend.gitBacked) and is the default primary
18	// when no backend is configured.
19	const BackendTypeGitBranch = "git-branch"
20	
21	// BackendTypeGitRefs is the built-in git-refs checkpoint backend: it stores the
22	// committed record as one git ref per checkpoint (refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/
23	// <id>) in this repo. Like git-branch it is git-backed, so it may be the primary;
24	// the two can run side by side (git-refs primary + git-branch mirror) during the
25	// branch->refs rollout, since the one-of-each-type rule permits distinct
26	// git-backed backends in the same topology.
27	const BackendTypeGitRefs = "git-refs"
28	
29	// OpenEnv carries the construction context a backend factory may need.
30	// Git-backed backends require Repo and use Refs/BlobFetcher/RefFetcher; other
31	// backends ignore the git-shaped fields and read their own configuration from cfg.
32	type OpenEnv struct {
33		Repo        *git.Repository
34		BlobFetcher BlobFetchFunc
35		RefFetcher  RefFetchFunc
36		Refs        PersistentRefs
37	}
38	
39	// Factory constructs a persistent store for one backend type. cfg is the
40	// backend-specific JSON "config" block from settings (nil when absent).
41	type Factory func(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, cfg json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error)
42	
43	// registeredBackend is a factory plus the capabilities the topology layer needs.
44	type registeredBackend struct {
45		factory Factory
46		// gitBacked reports whether the backend stores the committed record in this
47		// repo's git object store. Only git-backed backends may be the primary,
48		// because the checkpoint lifecycle (resume bootstrap, doctor reconcile,
49		// explain tree-read, push, cleanup, pre-push OPF) drives the primary's record
50		// through the repo and its refs — see buildPrimary. A backend that is not
51		// git-backed has no such ref for those paths to operate on, so it is
52		// mirror-only (write fan-out) until that lifecycle moves behind the store.
53		// Whether a backend may be a *mirror* is governed separately by the
54		// one-of-each-type topology rule in buildMirrors, not by this flag (a
55		// git-backed backend can mirror alongside a different git-backed primary).
56		gitBacked bool
57	}
58	
59	var (
60		registryMu sync.RWMutex
61		// registry maps backend type to its factory and capabilities. Git-backed
62		// backends are built in (registered here). Other backends add themselves
63		// through Register — in practice only test-only backends do, via their
64		// RegisterForTesting helpers, so a production binary can never select them.
65		registry = map[string]registeredBackend{
66			BackendTypeGitBranch: {factory: gitBranchBackendFactory, gitBacked: true},
67			BackendTypeGitRefs:   {factory: gitRefsBackendFactory, gitBacked: true},
68		}
69	)
70	
71	// Register adds a non-git-backed backend factory under typ. Such backends can
72	// serve as mirrors but not as the primary (see registeredBackend.gitBacked).
73	// Git-backed backends are built in and not registered through this path. It
74	// panics on a duplicate type to surface wiring mistakes.
75	func Register(typ string, f Factory) {
76		registryMu.Lock()
77		defer registryMu.Unlock()
78		if _, exists := registry[typ]; exists {
79			panic(fmt.Sprintf("checkpoint: backend type %q already registered", typ))
80		}
81		registry[typ] = registeredBackend{factory: f, gitBacked: false}
82	}
83	
84	// lookupBackend returns the registered backend for typ, or a clear error
85	// (naming the registered types) when the type is unknown.
86	func lookupBackend(typ string) (registeredBackend, error) {
87		registryMu.RLock()
88		b, ok := registry[typ]
89		registryMu.RUnlock()
90		if !ok {
91			return registeredBackend{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown checkpoint backend type %q (registered: %s)", typ, registeredTypes())
92		}
93		return b, nil
94	}
95	
96	// build constructs the store for the named backend type.
97	func build(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, typ string, cfg json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {
98		b, err := lookupBackend(typ)
99		if err != nil {
100			return nil, err
101		}
102		store, err := b.factory(ctx, env, cfg)
103		if err != nil {
104			return nil, fmt.Errorf("construct %q checkpoint backend: %w", typ, err)
105		}
106		return store, nil
107	}
108	
109	func registeredTypes() string {
110		registryMu.RLock()
111		defer registryMu.RUnlock()
112		types := make([]string, 0, len(registry))
113		for t := range registry {
114			types = append(types, t)
115		}
116		sort.Strings(types)
117		return strings.Join(types, ", ")
118	}

122	func gitBranchBackendFactory(_ context.Context, env OpenEnv, _ json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {

124			return nil, errors.New("git-branch checkpoint backend requires a repository")
125		}

136	func gitRefsBackendFactory(_ context.Context, env OpenEnv, _ json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {

146		}

13	// OpenOptions configures Open. The zero value uses the default committed-ref
14	// topology and attaches no blob fetcher.
15	type OpenOptions struct {
16		// BlobFetcher is the CLI-level on-demand blob fetcher. The checkpoint
17		// package cannot resolve it itself, so the CLI layer injects it here and
18		// Open attaches it to the constructed store(s). nil leaves on-demand
19		// fetching off.
20		BlobFetcher BlobFetchFunc
21	
22		// RefFetcher is the CLI-level on-demand checkpoint-ref fetcher, used by the
23		// git-refs backend to resolve a checkpoint ref missing locally. nil leaves
24		// reads local-only; ignored by the git-branch backend.
25		RefFetcher RefFetchFunc
26	
27		// Refs overrides the default committed-ref topology. A non-nil value wins,
28		// e.g. attach pins reads to Primary via PrimaryAsRead().
29		Refs *PersistentRefs
30	}
31	
32	// PrimaryIsRefs reports whether the configured primary backend is the git-refs
33	// per-checkpoint store. It centralizes the topology check so push/pre-push code
34	// does not compare backend-type strings itself. A nil config (default) is the
35	// git-branch backend, so this returns false.
36	func PrimaryIsRefs(cfg *settings.CheckpointsConfig) bool {
37		return cfg != nil && cfg.Primary.Type == BackendTypeGitRefs
38	}
39	
40	// Stores is the facade returned by Open: the persistent store plus the git-only
41	// ephemeral (shadow-branch) capability and resolved committed-ref topology.
42	type Stores struct {
43		// Persistent is the committed store that serves permanent reads and writes.
44		Persistent PersistentStore
45	
46		ephemeral EphemeralStore
47		refs      PersistentRefs
48	}
49	
50	// Open resolves the checkpoint storage topology and constructs the backing
51	// store(s). It keeps ref resolution, backend selection, and blob-fetcher wiring
52	// in one place. The primary is built through the backend registry; with no
53	// checkpoints config it resolves to the git-branch backend with no mirrors, so
54	// default behavior is unchanged. When mirrors are configured, the persistent
55	// store is a fan-out wrapper (reads from primary, best-effort writes to mirrors).
56	//
57	// Backend selection is read via settings.LoadCheckpointsConfig, which resolves
58	// like settings.Load: from the context's worktree root if set, else relative to
59	// the current working directory — not from repo. Callers opening a repository
60	// that is not the cwd should wrap ctx with that worktree root (as dispatch does).
61	// Resolution is fail-soft: a missing or unreadable settings file yields the
62	// default git-branch backend with no mirrors, preserving default behavior.
63	func Open(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, opts OpenOptions) (*Stores, error) {
64		refs := resolveOpenRefs(ctx, opts)
65		env := OpenEnv{Repo: repo, BlobFetcher: opts.BlobFetcher, RefFetcher: opts.RefFetcher, Refs: refs}
66	
67		cfg, err := settings.LoadCheckpointsConfig(ctx)
68		if err != nil {
69			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve checkpoints config: %w", err)
70		}
71	
72		primaryType := resolvePrimaryType(cfg)
73		primary, err := buildPrimary(ctx, env, primaryType, primaryConfig(cfg))
74		if err != nil {
75			return nil, err
76		}
77		mirrors, err := buildMirrors(ctx, env, cfg, primaryType)
78		if err != nil {
79			return nil, err
80		}
81		writer := newFanoutStore(primary, mirrors)
82	
83		// Read routing: resolve id-keyed reads by the checkpoint's format across both
84		// git backends (a ULID lives in refs, a hex ID on the branch or a migrated
85		// ref), so a coexisting / mid-migration repo reads either format without
86		// reconfiguring. Writes still go through writer (configured primary + mirrors).
87		branchStore, refsStore, err := buildKindReadStores(ctx, env, primaryType, primary)
88		if err != nil {
89			return nil, err
90		}
91	
92		return &Stores{
93			Persistent: newKindRoutingStore(writer, branchStore, refsStore, primaryType),
94			ephemeral:  newEphemeralStore(repo, refs),
95			refs:       refs,
96		}, nil
97	}
98	
99	// buildKindReadStores returns the git-branch and git-refs read stores used for
100	// id-kind read routing, reusing the already-built primary for whichever kind it
101	// is and constructing the sibling. A non-branch/refs git-backed primary (not a
102	// real configuration today, since buildPrimary only accepts git-backed backends)
103	// yields both freshly built git stores.
104	func buildKindReadStores(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, primaryType string, primary PersistentStore) (branch, refs PersistentStore, err error) {
105		switch primaryType {
106		case BackendTypeGitBranch:
107			branch = primary
108			refs, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitRefs, nil)
109		case BackendTypeGitRefs:
110			refs = primary
111			branch, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitBranch, nil)
112		default:
113			if branch, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitBranch, nil); err == nil {
114				refs, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitRefs, nil)
115			}
116		}
117		return branch, refs, err
118	}
119	
120	// resolvePrimaryType returns the configured primary backend type, defaulting to
121	// the git-branch backend when none is configured.
122	func resolvePrimaryType(cfg *settings.CheckpointsConfig) string {
123		if cfg != nil && cfg.Primary.Type != "" {
124			return cfg.Primary.Type
125		}
126		return BackendTypeGitBranch
127	}
128	
129	// primaryConfig returns the primary backend's config block, if any.
130	func primaryConfig(cfg *settings.CheckpointsConfig) json.RawMessage {
131		if cfg == nil {
132			return nil

137	// buildPrimary constructs the primary persistent store. The primary must be a
138	// git-backed backend: attach, resume, push, doctor, cleanup, and OPF all drive
139	// the primary's record through the repo and its refs, so a non-git-backed
140	// primary is rejected rather than silently half-supported.
141	func buildPrimary(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, typ string, raw json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {
142		b, err := lookupBackend(typ)
143		if err != nil {
144			return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.primary: %w", err)
145		}
146		if !b.gitBacked {
147			return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.primary.type %q cannot be the primary: only git-backed backends (e.g. %q) may be the primary", typ, BackendTypeGitBranch)
148		}
149		return build(ctx, env, typ, raw)
150	}

152	// buildMirrors constructs the mirror writers. Each backend type may appear at
153	// most once across the topology (primary + mirrors), so a mirror cannot reuse
154	// the primary's type or another mirror's. This is the conservative form of "no
155	// two backends may write the same target": today two backends of the same type
156	// share the same refs/storage, so a duplicate type is a guaranteed collision
157	// (e.g. a git-branch mirror under a git-branch primary would double-write the v1
158	// branch). A future per-mirror config (same backend type pointed at a distinct
159	// repo/refs) could relax this; for now it is one of each type.
160	func buildMirrors(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, cfg *settings.CheckpointsConfig, primaryType string) ([]Writer, error) {
161		if cfg == nil || len(cfg.Mirrors) == 0 {
162			return nil, nil
163		}
164		seen := map[string]bool{primaryType: true}
165		mirrors := make([]Writer, 0, len(cfg.Mirrors))
166		for i, m := range cfg.Mirrors {
167			if _, err := lookupBackend(m.Type); err != nil {
168				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: %w", i, err)
169			}
170			if seen[m.Type] {
171				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: backend type %q is already used by the primary or another mirror; each backend type may appear at most once", i, m.Type)
172			}
173			seen[m.Type] = true
174			store, err := build(ctx, env, m.Type, m.Config)
175			if err != nil {
176				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: %w", i, err)
177			}
178			mirrors = append(mirrors, store)
179		}
180		return mirrors, nil
181	}

782		var opts EnableOptions
783		var ignoreUntracked bool
784		var agentName string
785		var bootstrapOpts GitHubBootstrapOptions
786		var insecureHTTPAuth bool
787	
788		cmd := &cobra.Command{
789			Use:   "enable",
790			Short: "Enable Entire in current repository",
791			Long: `Enable Entire with session tracking for your AI agent workflows.
792	
793	If Entire is not yet configured, this runs the full configuration flow.
794	If Entire is already configured but disabled, this re-enables it.
795	
796	If the current directory is not a git repository, Entire can initialize one
797	for you and (optionally) create a matching GitHub repository via the gh CLI.`,
798			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) (runErr error) {
799				ctx := cmd.Context()
800				// Best-effort: after a successful enable, tell the backend which repo
801				// was enabled so the web onboarding reflects it (and we can warn when
802				// the GitHub App can't reach it). Registered first so it runs LAST
803				// (defers are LIFO) — after any bootstrap finalize that creates the
804				// GitHub repo and pushes, by which point an origin remote exists.
805				defer func() {
806					if runErr != nil {
807						return
808					}
809					reportRepoEnabled(ctx, insecureHTTPAuth)
810				}()
811				// Check if we're in a git repository first. If not, offer to
812				// bootstrap one (git init + optional GitHub repo). If the user
813				// declines, fall back to the legacy prerequisite error.
814				//
815				// The bootstrap runs in two phases: phase 1 (git init + identity
816				// + gather GitHub choices) before agent setup, phase 2
817				// (initial commit + gh repo create + push) after agent setup so
818				// the initial commit captures the .entire/, .claude/, hooks, and
819				// settings files that setup writes.
820				var bootstrap *bootstrapState
821				if _, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx); err != nil {
822					bootstrapOpts.Yes = opts.Yes
823					state, bootstrapErr := runGitHubBootstrapInit(ctx, cmd.OutOrStdout(), cmd.ErrOrStderr(), bootstrapOpts)
824					if errors.Is(bootstrapErr, errBootstrapDeclined) {
825						fmt.Fprintln(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "Not a git repository. Please run 'entire enable' from within a git repository, or pass --init-repo to initialize one here.")
826						return NewSilentError(errors.New("not a git repository"))
827					}
828					if errors.Is(bootstrapErr, errBootstrapInterrupted) {
829						fmt.Fprintln(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "Bootstrap cancelled. A local git repository has been initialized but setup didn't complete. Run `entire enable` again to continue.")
830						return NewSilentError(errors.New("bootstrap interrupted"))
831					}
832					if bootstrapErr != nil {
833						return bootstrapErr
834					}
835					bootstrap = state
836					// Let the enable flow know that we'll be handling the final
837					// "done" summary from the bootstrap finalize step.
838					opts.SuppressDoneMessage = true
839					// Re-check after bootstrap.
840					if _, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx); err != nil {
841						return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap finished but no git repository detected: %w", err)
842					}
843					// Visual separator between bootstrap init and agent setup.
844					printBootstrapSection(cmd.OutOrStdout(), "Enabling Entire")
845					// On the way out (if setup succeeded), create the initial
846					// commit and push to the GitHub repo. If setup returned an
847					// error, skip the finalize — the user can fix the issue and
848					// re-run; any partial state is just untracked files.
849					defer func() {
850						if runErr != nil || bootstrap == nil {
851							return
852						}
853						if err := runGitHubBootstrapFinalize(ctx, cmd.OutOrStdout(), bootstrap); err != nil {
854							runErr = err
855						}
856					}()
857				}
858	
859				if err := validateSetupFlags(opts.UseLocalSettings, opts.UseProjectSettings); err != nil {
860					return err
861				}
862

866				external.DiscoverAndRegisterAlways(ctx)

869				if cmd.Flags().Changed(agentFlagName) && agentName == "" {
870					printMissingAgentError(cmd.ErrOrStderr())
871					return NewSilentError(errors.New("missing agent name"))
872				}
873	
874				if agentName != "" {
875					ag, err := agent.Get(types.AgentName(agentName))
876					if err != nil {
877						printWrongAgentError(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), agentName)
878						return NewSilentError(errors.New("wrong agent name"))
879					}

881					// affecting other agents. Unlike the interactive path, it does not

884				}

content.text:
Both options are implemented, verified end-to-end against the real binary, and the full unit suite (7613 tests) plus lint pass.

## What I built

The git-refs backend was already fully wired to *run* — the only missing piece was a config *writer*. I added that as a single `--checkpoint-backend` flag plus a first-run selector.

**Option 1 — shared flag on `enable` + `configure`** (covers both scenarios):
- `entire configure --checkpoint-backend refs` — the existing-repo path (canonical home for non-agent settings).
- `entire enable --checkpoint-backend refs` — works on both fresh repos and already-set-up repos (the already-set-up branch now behaves like `configure`), and on the `--agent` non-interactive path.
- Accepts friendly `branch`/`refs` and canonical `git-branch`/`git-refs` (trimmed, case-insensitive).

**Option 3 — interactive selector, branch as default**:
- On the first interactive setup, `runEnableInteractive` prompts with **Branch (default)** / **Refs (experimental)**. An explicit flag skips the prompt; non-interactive / `--yes` / not-first-run keep the default silently. Uses `NewAccessibleForm` (ACCESSIBLE-mode safe), and choosing the default writes nothing (keeps `settings.json` clean).

**Verified behavior:**
- Invalid value fails fast before any repo bootstrap/hook install: `invalid --checkpoint-backend: unknown checkpoint backend type "bogus" (registered: git-branch, git-refs)`.
- Writes/round-trips correctly through `settings.json` and `--local` → `settings.local.json`; switching back to `branch` overrides cleanly.
- Fresh enable without the flag writes **no** `checkpoints` block.

**Key design choices baked in:**
- Only git-backed backends can be primary — enforced via a new exported `checkpoint.ValidatePrimaryBackend`, so the error list stays in sync with the registry.
- `applyCheckpointBackend` preserves existing mirrors but drops one that would collide with the new primary (the one-of-each-type rule).
- Switching primary on an existing repo is safe — old checkpoints stay readable via the existing kind-routing; no migration needed.

**Files:** `checkpoint/registry.go` (+validator/test), `checkpoint_backend.go` (new helpers), `checkpoint_backend_test.go` (new), `setup.go` (flag, wiring, extracted `runEnableOnConfiguredRepo` to keep complexity in check).

Two follow-ups I deliberately left out of scope (say the word if you want them):
- **Downgrade safety**: refs→branch mirror-push isn't implemented upstream yet, so switching *back* off refs after pushing refs-format checkpoints has the known remote-visibility caveat.
- **Docs**: I didn't touch `docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md` since this is the experiments tree — happy to add a short "selecting a backend" note if you want it.

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than

skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

Build, lint, and tests all pass. Here's the `/simplify` result.

## Applied (3 fixes)

1. **De-duplicated the "primary must be git-backed" rule** (`checkpoint/open.go`) — flagged by both the *reuse* and *altitude* agents. `buildPrimary` now delegates to the new `ValidatePrimaryBackend` instead of re-implementing the `lookupBackend` + `!gitBacked` check. This single-sources the rule, drops a redundant registry lookup, and fixes an **already-diverged** error message (the two copies listed different example backends). Updated the doc comment to reflect it's now the source of truth.

2. **Simplified the mirror-drop loop** (`checkpoint_backend.go`) — *simplification* agent. Replaced the 9-line guarded `make`/append/reassign with one `slices.DeleteFunc`. Behavior-identical (nil stays nil; `mirrors` is `omitempty` anyway; `s` is never aliased at the call sites).

3. **Dropped the redundant `backend string` param** from `updateCheckpointBackend` (`checkpoint_backend.go`) — *simplification* agent. It now reads `opts.CheckpointBackend` directly, matching its sibling `updateStrategyOptions(ctx, w, opts)` and removing a param that could silently diverge from `opts`. Updated 2 call sites + 3 test calls.

## Skipped (noted)

- **Efficiency** — nothing. The double validation (fail-fast before bootstrap, then at apply) is intentional and pure/cheap; the per-flag-group load+save is the established `update*` pattern, not a regression.
- **Vocabulary seam** (altitude, low-priority) — flag/prompt say `branch`/`refs` but a typo's error lists canonical `git-branch`/`git-refs`. The agent confirmed the alias mapping belongs in the CLI layer (not the registry), and the error is still actionable. Left as-is to keep the change tight.
- **`loadTargetSettings` helper across all 5 `update*` functions** (reuse) — a real DRY opportunity, but it's a pre-existing pattern spanning code outside this diff.
- **Prompt-default-writes-nothing vs flag-writes-explicit-block** asymmetry (altitude) — principled (keeps fresh settings pristine; explicit downgrade *must* write a block), not an accidental special case.

The layering (`resolve` → `apply` → `applyFlag`/`updateCheckpointBackend`) was confirmed by two agents to map to genuinely distinct call sites — not collapsed.

## Summary

The git-refs checkpoint backend was already fully wired to *run*, but had no config **writer** — it could only be turned on via `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_PRIMARY` or by hand-editing `.entire/settings.json`. This adds a simple selection path for both an existing repo and initial enable.

## What's new

- **`--checkpoint-backend branch|refs`** (also accepts canonical `git-branch`/`git-refs`) on both `entire enable` and `entire configure`.
  - Covers fresh repos, the `--agent` non-interactive path, and already-set-up repos (`enable` on a configured repo behaves like `configure`).
- **Interactive selector on first-time setup** — prompts for the backend, defaulting to **branch**. Choosing the default writes no config block, keeping `settings.json` pristine (an explicit flag always writes the block). Uses `NewAccessibleForm` so it respects `ACCESSIBLE=1`.
- **Up-front validation** — a bad value fails before any repo bootstrap / hook install, via a new `checkpoint.ValidatePrimaryBackend`, which is now the single source of the "primary must be git-backed" rule (`buildPrimary` delegates to it).
- **Safe primary switch** — preserves existing mirrors, dropping only one that would collide with the new primary (one-of-each-type rule). Existing hex-ID checkpoints stay readable via kind-routing; no migration needed.

## Verified

- Full `mise run check`: fmt clean, lint 0 issues, unit + 59 integration + 4 e2e canary tests pass.
- Exercised the real binary end-to-end: invalid value fails fast; `configure` before enable is rejected; refs written and round-tripped through `settings.json` and `--local`; downgrade back to branch overrides correctly; fresh enable without the flag writes no `checkpoints` block.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- **Downgrade data-safety**: refs→branch mirror-push isn't implemented upstream yet, so switching *off* refs after pushing refs-format checkpoints has the known remote-visibility caveat.
- Docs (`sessions-and-checkpoints.md`) not updated — happy to add a short "selecting a backend" note if wanted.
